en: So now in this section, you saw how a
workflow could look like in code and how it
could look like when you build it visually.
And
I can't emphasize it enough, the core
takeaway is that a workflow is a sequence of
steps, and therefore it's often very useful
because it turns out that many problems,
especially many business problems,
are just a sequence of steps that should
always be executed in the same repeatable
way.
There also are situations where you want an
agent, as you'll also see later, especially
if the input is dynamic, if it's a chat
message or an email, for example. But for
many problems, the sequence of steps is
deterministic. That is when you should
consider building a workflow instead of
using an agent and hoping that it gets the
sequence of steps right. There is no reason
to hope if you can hardcode it instead.
Now, obviously,
you can build way more complex workflows,
both with code and also visually, but as
mentioned, this is not the focus of the
course. The focus of this course is to give
you an overview of what the general idea is
and how you should think about workflows
versus agents and how to build each and use
each.
